item.title: Fable Five and the Starting Gun of AI Governance
item.description: The US government ordered Anthropic to pull its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models globally citing national security, marking the first executive-branch model shutdown in history. Also covered: DiffusionGemma's 4x speed gains, WorkBench's two-year agent progress report, and LLM judge reliability failures.

item.title: When AI Builds Itself: Recursive Development and the Accountability Gap
item.description: Anthropic's institute publishes internal data showing 8x engineer code productivity as AI accelerates its own development; paired with papers on evaluation blind spots, model collapse epidemiology, and error severity, the week's theme is the collapse of inherited accountability proxies across open source, enterprise, and education.

item.title: Anthropic at $47B and the Revenue Inflection
item.description: Anthropic closes a $65B Series H at a $900B valuation with $47B in run-rate revenue, ships Opus 4.8 and dynamic workflows; plus Cognition's $26B Series D, the Google OS demo debunking, AI jobs apocalypse reversal, and research on CUDA kernel silent failures and LLM interpretability.

item.title: Erdős Falls, Google IO, and the AI Restructuring Wave
item.description: An OpenAI reasoning model disproves an eighty-year-old conjecture in discrete geometry for under $1000; Google deploys Gemini across consumer, developer, and science products at I/O; Anthropic locks in $1.25B/month in compute via an xAI deal disclosed in SpaceX's IPO filing. Plus Intuit cuts 3,000 jobs, students boo AI commencement speakers, and what the collision of these timelines actually means.

item.title: Supply chain, open ecosystems, and the reliability gap
item.description: A TanStack npm supply chain attack threatening OpenAI's signing certificates opens a week of AI news about where the field's reliability boundaries actually are — from contaminated benchmarks and invisible orchestrators to clinical AI errors documented by auditors and a new governance framework for the age of powerful AI.

item.title: The twenty twenty-eight threshold
item.description: Jack Clark assigns sixty percent or better odds to fully autonomous AI R&D by end of twenty twenty-eight — this week covers that analysis alongside new benchmarks for military AI compliance, AIGC detector evasion, hidden fine-tuning detection, and what the cumulative safety research picture implies for the governance window.
